slot.brief: Compare rms speeds of two gases at the same temperature using v ∝ 1/√M.

stem: Ammonia and hydrogen sulfide gases are maintained at the same temperature. Their molar masses are $17\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$ and $34\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$, respectively. What is the ratio of their rms speeds, $v_{\text{NH}_3}/v_{\text{H}_2\text{S}}$?

verdicts.working: At the same temperature, rms speed is inversely proportional to the square root of molar mass. Hence the ratio is √(34/17) = √2.

working:
$v_{\mathrm{rms}}\propto\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{M}}$ at the same temperature.
$\dfrac{v_{\text{NH}_3}}{v_{\text{H}_2\text{S}}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{M_{\text{H}_2\text{S}}}{M_{\text{NH}_3}}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{34}{17}}=\sqrt{2}$

Independent check: At the same temperature, rms speed is inversely proportional to the square root of molar mass. Hence the ratio is √(34/17) = √2.
